newsitem.title: USA: First relief shipment heads to Cuba on Saturday.
newsitem.headline: First relief shipment heads to Cuba on Saturday.

text.p: The first planeload of relief supplies to help Cubans devastated by Hurricane Lili will fly to Cuba on Saturday, a Catholic Church official said on Friday.
U.S. authorities have waived a ban on direct flights from the United States to Cuba to allow the humanitarian mission.

"We have 70,000 lb (31,750 kg) of milk, rice and beans, already palletized and wrapped ready for the plane," said Peter Coats, the special assistant to the director of Catholic Charities for the Archdiocease of Miami.
The flight will also carry some samples of tarps that can be used for temporary shelter and repairs.
Coats refused to identify the airline that will carry the cargo and the freight forwarder that has helped with the handling. "All we can say is that they are very, very generous people," he said.
The Cuban community in Miami has traditionally been divided about sending humanitarian aid to Cuba. Some feel strongly that it assists the Castro government.
Some of the boxes are marked with the word "exilio," indicating they are coming from the Cuban exile community. Coats said the labels should not cause a problem.
"We understand that the Castro governement has concerns about overtly political materials on the boxes and cans. We don't consider exilio to be a political statement," he said.
Hurricane Lili swept across the communist-ruled nation last week, flattening more than 2,000 homes and damaging fields of sugar cane, citrus and other crops.

The Catholic Charities has collected close to 300,000 lb (136,000 kg) of supplies, mostly food, and about $30,000, Coats said. They hope to have another flight leave by the end of next week and have all the materials in Cuba in a month.
The money will be used for supplies that have not been donated or to pay for flights if the group can not get flights donated, Coats said.
The Catholic Church's Caritas will handle the distribution in Cuba, Coats said. Three Catholic officials will accompany the flight, he said.
